nodes.name: In situ selenylation to NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthetic route, 15 mg of Se (stoichiometric ratio of Se/Ni = 1:1) powder was added to 30 mL of deionized water containing 0.070 g NaBH4 to obtain a clear NaHSe solution under stirring. The prepared NaHSe solution was then added into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave (50 mL). Then, the NiO/CP was immersed into the solution, and the autoclave was heated in the oven at 180 °C for 12 h. After the autoclave was cooled to room temperature naturally, the produced NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP was removed, washed with water and ethanol three times, and dried at room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO/CP shows uniform vertical nanoflakes with thickness ≈30 nm and lateral length ≈1 μm; NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP retains integral nanoflake array morphology after selenylation but with coarse uneven surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a,b shows the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of NiO/CP at different magnifications. NiO nanoflakes were uniformly and vertically anchored on the surface of CP (Figure 1a). These NiO nanoflakes had a thickness of ≈30 nm and a lateral length of ≈1 μm (Figure 1b). ... For the NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP hybrid, the SEM image in Figure 1c reveals that the integral nanoflake array morphology was not changed after selenylation. However, the surfaces of the nanoflakes were coarse and uneven (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms porous nanoflake composed of interconnected nanoparticles; SAED pattern indexed to polycrystalline NiSe and Ni0.85Se.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) characterization further confirmed the porous nanoflake is composed of interconnected nanoparticles (Figure 1e). The corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (inset) can be indexed to polycrystalline NiSe and Ni0.85Se as marked.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows overlapping lattice fringes with spacings of 0.195 nm and 0.116 nm indexed to (131) and (211) planes of NiSe and Ni0.85Se respectively, confirming heterostructure formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1f), the overlapping lattice fringes with spacings of 0.195 and 0.116 nm can be indexed to the (131) and (211) crystal planes of NiSe and Ni0.85Se, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe/CP shows hexagonal NiSe phase (JCPDS 18-0887) with peaks at 32.8°, 44.5°, 49.5°, 59.2°, 60.9°; Ni0.85Se/CP shows Ni0.85Se phase (JCPDS 18-0888) with peaks at 33.1°, 44.9°, 50.4°, 60.2°, 61.7°, 69.6°, 71.4°; NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP (Ni/Se=1:1) shows mixed phase with 64.7% NiSe content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the molar ratio of Ni/Se is relatively large (2:1), the obtained product is NiSe. ... In contrast, when the molar ratio of Ni/Se is relatively low (1:2), pure Ni0.85Se is produced. ... a mixed phase of NiSe-Ni0.85Se can form when the molar ratio of Ni/Se is moderate (1:1).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP shows Ni 2p peaks at 852.6, 869.8 eV and 856.1, 873.6 eV for NiSe, satellite peaks at 861.7, 880.2 eV for Ni²⁺; Se 3d peaks at 54.4, 55.3 eV and 58.8 eV for SeOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the XPS spectrum of NiSe-Ni0.85Se, the two peaks at 852.6 and 869.8 eV correspond to Ni2p₃/₂ and Ni2p₁/₂, respectively (Figure 2c). Another set of Ni2p peaks at 856.1 and 873.6 eV correspond to Ni2p₃/₂ and Ni2p₁/₂ of NiSe, respectively. The Se 3d peaks (Figure 2d) at binding energies of 54.4 and 55.3 eV correspond to Se3d₅/₂ and Se3d₃/₂, respectively, and the peak at 58.8 eV suggests the existence of surface Se species in a high oxide state (SeOₓ).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values calculated from CV: NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP = 35.9 mF cm⁻² (OER), NiSe/CP = 9.5 mF cm⁻² (OER), Ni0.85Se/CP = 5.9 mF cm⁻² (OER); NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP also shows superior ECSA and RF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of the various electrodes were calculated to be 35.9, 9.5, and 5.9 mF cm⁻² for NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP, NiSe/CP, and Ni0.85Se/CP, respectively (Figure 3d).

nodes.characterization_summary: OER Rct: NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP = 245 Ω, NiSe/CP ≈324 Ω, Ni0.85Se/CP ≈385 Ω; HER Rct (at 100 mV overpotential): NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP = 59 Ω, NiSe/CP = 81 Ω, Ni0.85Se/CP = 142 Ω.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3e reveals that the charge-transfer resistance (Rct) values of NiSe/CP, Ni0.85Se/CP, and NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP are ≈324, 385, and 245 Ω respectively. ... NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP showed a lower Rct in the Nyquist plots (59 Ω) than NiSe/CP (81 Ω) and Ni0.85Se/CP (142 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Sheet resistance: NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP = 3.43 kΩ sq⁻¹, NiSe/CP = 5.15 kΩ sq⁻¹, Ni0.85Se/CP = 5.72 kΩ sq⁻¹, confirming highest conductivity for heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The four-point probe system measurements also revealed resistance values of 3.43, 5.15, and 5.72 kΩ sq⁻¹ for NiSe-Ni0.85Se/CP, NiSe/CP, and Ni0.85Se/CP respectively (Figure S10, Supporting Information).
